title.en: 에 vs 에서 for places and times

summary.en: When a place takes 에 (destination or static location) versus 에서 (where an action happens or 'from').

body.en:
English uses 'in' or 'at' for both 'staying in Seoul' and 'working in Seoul', whereas Korean separates static location/destination (*에*) from the stage of an active event (*에서*).

Use *에* for three core jobs: static existence with *있어요* / *없어요* / *계세요* (*책상 위에 있어요*, 'it is on the desk'), destination with motion verbs like *가다* / *오다* (*서울에 왔어요*, 'came to Seoul'), and points in time (*아침 여덟 시에*, 'at eight in the morning'; *금요일에*, 'on Friday'). Note that *오늘* ('today'), *내일* ('tomorrow'), and *어제* ('yesterday') stand alone without *에*.

Use *에서* whenever an action takes place inside a space (*주방에서 빵을 구워요*, 'bake bread in the kitchen'; *시청에서 일해요*, 'work at City Hall'), and also for 'from' a starting point (*기차역에서 걸어왔어요*, 'walked from the train station').
